sections.html:
Sandy is a city in Salt Lake County, tucked against the Wasatch Mountains, roughly 13 miles from downtown Salt Lake. The 2020 census counted 96,904 people, a rise of 10.8 percent over the 87,461 counted in 2010. The real surge happened earlier. Sandy went from 6,438 residents in 1970 to 52,210 in 1980, and a big portion of today's houses went up in that stretch of fast building.

YearSandy population
19706,438
198052,210
201087,461
202096,904

Think about that history before you pick an asking price. Roofs, furnaces and water heaters installed in the same years age together, and an inspector working for the buyer will check each one.

Sandy's eastern edge rises into the foothills. Its western edge is flat valley floor, and the Jordan River marks part of that boundary. Lots, views and drainage change from one side to the other, so visitors to a hillside home ask different things than visitors to a home by the river. Canyons School District has been the main district since the 2009-10 school year. Boundaries move now and then, so ask the district which school an address feeds before you promise anything to a buyer.

Freeway access comes from I-15 on the western side, with exits at 9000 South, 10600 South and 11400 South. State Street is U.S. Route 89, parallel to the freeway, while State Route 209 goes east and west. Four TRAX Blue Line light rail stops sit inside Sandy. UTA buses fill in the rest, and one seasonal ski route heads for Alta and Snowbird.

  • Historic Sandy at 9000 South
  • Sandy Expo at 9375 South
  • Sandy Civic Center at 10000 South
  • Crescent View at 11400 South

A short walk to a station or an easy hop to the freeway belongs near the top of your description. A house on a loud arterial street will draw comments about traffic, so decide ahead of time what you will say.

The Cairns is the city center redevelopment plan, a 25-year effort covering about 1,100 acres. The master plan was adopted in January 2017 and divides the area into three villages: Central, South and East. The South Village includes City Hall and the Hale Centre Theatre, and the East Village is a transit-oriented area around the Sandy Civic Center TRAX station.

America First Field opened on October 8, 2008 and hosts Real Salt Lake and Utah Royals FC. We do not predict what projects like these do to home prices. The honest pitch is simple: a long-range plan and several big developments are under way near the middle of town, and buyers can decide what that is worth.

sections.h2: Foundation cracks, the canyon and the fault
sections.html:
Little Cottonwood Canyon gave Sandy its mining past and now leads to the Alta and Snowbird ski areas. State Route 210 climbs the canyon for about 8.3 miles at an average grade of 9.2 percent, and Alta averages around 550 inches of snow a year. Snow piles up on roofs there, so an older roof gets a close look.

The city is also part of the Wasatch Front, where the Wasatch Fault stretches about 240 miles in 10 segments, five of them active. Around 80 percent of Utahns live along it. On March 18, 2020 a 5.7 quake near Magna did moderate damage across the valley.

Hairline cracks in a foundation or chimney tend to appear in a buyer's inspection report. A cash buyer sees the house as it is today and prices the work into the offer, so you skip the contractor bids.

Sandy's city government runs building permits, code enforcement, trash pickup, a bulk waste program, recycling and utility billing, and it licenses pets and businesses. If you finished a basement or built a deck, call Community Development and ask whether that project needed a permit.

  • Check for code violations on the city's code violation page.
  • Haul out old furniture and junk through the Bulk Waste program.
  • Settle the last utility bill and close any open permits.

An unclosed permit or an old violation can hold up a sale. Heirs, and owners who bought a half-finished project, often find a cash buyer easier than a punch list and a public listing.

Salt Lake County does the assessing and billing for Sandy. Assessed value is set each January 1. Owner-occupied homes get a 45 percent exemption covering the buildings and as much as one acre. The bill must be paid by November 30.

Pay late and you owe 2.5 percent on top. Clear the full balance by January 31 and that charge shrinks to 1 percent. Parcels still unpaid after that go to the county tax sale in late May. When you sell partway through a year, ask your title company how the tax is split between you and the buyer, and get the number on paper before closing day.

Your valuation notice arrives in late July. The Board of Equalization hears appeals from August 1 through September 15, or for 45 days after the mailing when that runs later. Submit a BE01 form with proof, for example nearby sales, repair quotes or photos of damage.

Filing works online, by mail to 2001 South State Street, or at room N3-300 in the Government Center. Pull your proof together early so September is not a scramble.

Listing the usual way brings deep cleaning, repairs, photography, open houses, an appraisal and an inspection followed by repair demands. A cash offer cuts most of that out. You describe the property, we respond with an offer, and you choose the closing day that fits your move. A title company still handles the closing paperwork.

Gather a few items first: install dates for the roof, furnace and water heater, any permit records, a recent utility bill and, if a mortgage exists, the payoff amount from your lender. With those in hand the offer comes faster and fits the house better.

Once you accept an offer, a title company opens the file and searches the ownership record for liens or unpaid bills. You sign the deed and settlement papers, any mortgage balance is paid from the proceeds, and the remainder goes to you. The deed is recorded with the county, and you hand over the keys.

Bring a government photo ID and the garage and door openers. If tenants live there, bring copies of their leases. A quick walk through the rooms beforehand helps you remember what is staying and what is not.

sections.h2: List, sell by owner or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
Pick based on how the house looks and how fast you must move. A listing suits a tidy home and an owner who can live through weeks of showings.

A cash offer fits a home that needs work, an inherited property, a house with tenants, or a tight deadline. Ask for our number, set it beside what a listing would likely net you, and walk away if it does not work. It costs nothing to ask.

faqs.q: Which county is Sandy, Utah in?
faqs.a: Sandy is in Salt Lake County, and the county offices handle assessments, tax bills and appeals.

faqs.q: What school district is Sandy in?
faqs.a: Canyons School District has been the main district since 2009-10. Ask the district about any particular address.

faqs.q: When are Sandy property taxes due?
faqs.a: The deadline is November 30. Anything unpaid is delinquent December 1, and paying everything by January 31 lowers the penalty to 1 percent.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sandy home's valuation?
faqs.a: Go to the Salt Lake County Board of Equalization from August 1 to September 15, or 45 days after your notice if that ends later. Bring the BE01 form and your proof of value.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Sandy house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The offer reflects the house as it stands, so the roof, furnace or foundation can wait.
